meanings.usage: 用来描述人或交通工具按照约定时间到达或完成的状态
指长期的环境影响或反复经历形成的固定思维、行为模式

meanings.meaning: 不可动摇的，坚定不移的
meanings.usage: 常用来修饰信念、信仰、决心等抽象名词，表示其非常稳固
作“扰乱”义时，宾语多为服务、计划、系统等事物
用来修饰动作或状态，表示其只持续有限的时间
作名词时可指特快列车、快递服务；也可作形容词表示“特快的”
用来强调数量少、程度轻，放在名词前修饰

meanings.meaning: 给（某人以……）印象，让（某人）觉得
meanings.usage: 常用结构为it strikes sb as + adj. 表示“某人觉得某事怎么样”
用来描述事物或情况不符合常理、令人疑惑
后可接that从句或者on/upon sth，表示对某事进行深入思考
可作不及物动词，表示动作缓慢、浪费时间
常用结构it dawns on sb that... 表示“某人逐渐明白某事”
表示刚刚达到某个最低程度，暗含数量少、程度低的含义
常见搭配为lodge a complaint/protest/claim against sb
宾语多为服务、活动、航班等，表示其暂时停止运营或开展

phrases.usage: 表示利用某种有利条件、机会或服务，中性用法

examples.en: You should take advantage of the free library resources to improve your English.
examples.zh: 你应该利用免费的图书馆资源来提升你的英语水平。

examples.en: Many tourists take advantage of the low season to travel at a lower cost.
examples.zh: 很多游客利用淡季以更低的成本出行。

phrases.usage: 被动语态中表示“被耽搁、被延误”，主语通常是交通工具、行程等

examples.en: We were held up for two hours on the highway because of the car accident.
examples.zh: 因为车祸，我们在高速公路上被耽搁了两个小时。

examples.en: The project was held up by a lack of funding.
examples.zh: 这个项目因为资金短缺被延误了。

phrases.usage: 表示某人逐渐明白、突然意识到某个之前没注意到的事实，主语通常是it

examples.en: It dawned on me that I had left my keys at the office when I got home.
examples.zh: 我到家的时候才突然意识到我把钥匙落在办公室了。

examples.en: It finally dawned on him that all the suggestions his parents gave were for his own good.
examples.zh: 他终于明白父母给的所有建议都是为了他好。

phrases.usage: 表示“以书面形式、白纸黑字”，强调内容有正式的文字记录，不容否认

examples.en: I want the terms of our agreement in black and white to avoid future disputes.
examples.zh: 我希望我们的协议条款白纸黑字写下来，避免未来产生纠纷。

examples.en: You can't deny you made the promise—it's here in black and white.
examples.zh: 你不能否认你许下过这个承诺——这里白纸黑字写着呢。

phrases.usage: 表示正式向相关方提出投诉，语气比较正式

examples.en: If the noise from the construction site continues, I will lodge a complaint with the property management.
examples.zh: 如果工地的噪音还继续，我就要向物业投诉了。

examples.en: Many customers lodged complaints against the restaurant for its poor hygiene conditions.
examples.zh: 很多顾客投诉这家餐厅卫生条件很差。

phrases.usage: 表示某人觉得某事很奇怪、反常

examples.en: It strikes me as odd that he never mentions his family when we talk.
examples.zh: 我们聊天的时候他从来没提过他的家人，我觉得很奇怪。

examples.en: Her sudden change of attitude struck everyone as odd.
examples.zh: 她突然的态度转变让所有人都觉得反常。

phrases.usage: 表示忍不住、情不自禁做某事

examples.en: I can't help laughing every time I watch that comedy show.
examples.zh: 我每次看那个喜剧节目都忍不住笑。

examples.en: She couldn't help crying when she heard the bad news.
examples.zh: 她听到这个坏消息的时候忍不住哭了。

grammar.title: 部分倒装 (Partial Inversion)
grammar.structure: Negative word/phrase + 助动词/情态动词 + 主语 + 谓语动词剩余部分
grammar.definition: 将谓语的一部分（如助动词、情态动词）放到主语前面的倒装结构，通常用于否定词或半否定词放在句首的情况 当neither, nor, never, hardly, seldom等否定或半否定含义的词/短语放在句首时，句子需要使用部分倒装，来强调否定的含义

examples.en: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
examples.zh: 当火车在沿线几英里外的小站威德利停靠时，我也没有感到惊讶。

examples.en: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset in my life.
examples.zh: 我这辈子从来没见过这么美的日落。

examples.en: Seldom does he go to bed before 11 o'clock on weekdays.
examples.zh: 工作日他很少在11点前睡觉。

grammar.title: 情态动词表推测 (Modal Verbs for Deduction)
grammar.structure: 情态动词 + 动词原形（对现在的推测）/ have done（对过去的推测）
grammar.definition: 用must, might, may, can't等情态动词对现在或过去的情况进行可能性判断 must表示非常肯定的推测“一定”，might/may表示可能性较低的推测“可能”，can't表示否定推测“不可能”

examples.en: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
examples.zh: 我心想，除了我之外，肯定还有很多人想要享受这项优质的服务。

examples.en: The ground is wet. It must have rained last night.
examples.zh: 地面是湿的，昨晚肯定下雨了。

examples.en: He might come to the party tonight, but I'm not sure.
examples.zh: 他今晚可能会来派对，但我不确定。

patterns.pattern: We have learnt to expect that...

original.en: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
original.zh: 我们已经习惯于期待火车准点。

imitations.en: We have learnt to expect that the delivery will arrive within three working days.
imitations.zh: 我们已经习惯于期待快递会在三个工作日内送达。

imitations.en: We have learnt to expect that the coffee shop will be open at 7 a.m. every day.
imitations.zh: 我们已经习惯于期待这家咖啡店每天早上7点开门。

patterns.pattern: It suddenly dawned on me that...

original.en: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
original.zh: 我突然意识到，这趟快车并没有以90英里的时速在轨道上疾驰，而是只以30英里的时速突突地缓慢前进。

imitations.en: It suddenly dawned on me that I had signed up for the speech contest next week.
imitations.zh: 我突然想起我报名了下周的演讲比赛。

imitations.en: It suddenly dawned on me that the answer to the problem was much simpler than I thought.
imitations.zh: 我突然意识到这个问题的答案比我想的要简单得多。

patterns.pattern: There was a note of + 情绪名词 + in one's voice when...

original.en: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
original.zh: 我告诉他白纸黑字写在那儿的时候，声音里带着一丝得意。

imitations.en: There was a note of disappointment in her voice when she said she failed the exam.
imitations.zh: 她说自己考试没及格的时候，声音里带着一丝失望。

imitations.en: There was a note of excitement in his voice when he told us he got the offer.
imitations.zh: 他告诉我们他拿到录用通知的时候，声音里带着一丝兴奋。

lines.en: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
lines.zh: 我们已经习惯于相信火车总是准点的。

lines.en: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
lines.zh: 经过多年的适应，大多数人对火车时刻表产生了一种不可动摇的信念。

lines.en: Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be cancelled because of bad weather, but trains must be on time.
lines.zh: 轮船船期可能因风暴而推延，飞机航班可能因恶劣天气而取消，唯有火车必然是准点的。

lines.en: Only an exceptionally heavy snowfall might temporarily dislocate railway services.
lines.zh: 只有非同寻常的大雪才可能暂时打乱铁路运行。

lines.en: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
lines.zh: 因此，一旦铁路上真出了问题，人们便不加思索地责备铁路当局。

lines.en: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.
lines.zh: 事实上，差错很可能是我们自己，而不是铁路当局的。

lines.en: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.
lines.zh: 我查看了列车时刻表，满意地了解到有一趟去威斯特海温的快车。

lines.en: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted mere hour and seventeen minutes.
lines.zh: 这是趟直达车，旅途总共才需1小时17分钟。

lines.en: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
lines.zh: 上车后，我不禁注意到许多当地人也上了车。

lines.en: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.
lines.zh: 一开始，我并不感到奇怪，我想除我之外，想利用快车之便的也一定大有人在。

lines.en: I reflected that there must be a great many local people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
lines.zh: 火车开出几英里即在一个小站威德里停了下来。

lines.en: Neither was I surprise when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
lines.zh: 对此，我不觉得奇怪，因为即便是特别快车也可能被信号拦住。

lines.en: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
lines.zh: 但是，当火车一站接着一站往前蠕动时，我便产生了怀疑。

lines.en: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder, It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
lines.zh: 我突然感到这趟快车并没以时速90英里的速度呼啸前进，而是卟哧卟哧地向前爬行，时速仅30英里。1小时17分过去了，走了还不到一半路程。

lines.en: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.
lines.zh: 我问一位乘客，这是不是开往威斯特海温的那趟快车，他说从未听说过有这么一趟快车。

lines.en: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.
lines.zh: 我决定到目的地就给铁路部门提意见。

lines.en: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.
lines.zh: 两小时后，我气呼呼地同威斯特海温站站长说起此事。

lines.en: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.
lines.zh: 他说根本没有这趟车。

lines.en: When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.
lines.zh: 于是我借他本人的列车时刻表，我带着一种胜利者的调子告诉他那趟车白纸黑字。

lines.en: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
lines.zh: 明明白白印在时刻表上。

lines.en: Glancing at it briefly , he told me to look again.
lines.zh: 他迅速地扫视了一眼，让我再看一遍。

lines.en: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.
lines.zh: 一个小小的星形符号把我的目光引到了那页底部一个说明上。

lines.en: It said: 'This service has been suspended.'
lines.zh: 上面写着：“此趟列车暂停运行。”

questions.q: What was the mistake the author made?
questions.a: The mistake was his own: he trusted the timetable and boarded the 'express train to Westhaven' that, according to a footnote, had been suspended, because he failed to notice a tiny asterisk.
questions.aZh: 错在作者自己：他轻信时刻表，上了那趟据脚注所说'已暂停运行'的'开往西黑文的快车'，只因他没有注意到那个小小的星号。
questions.hint: 出处：课文末尾 'A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote…It said: "This service has been suspended."'

questions.q: What did the timetable tell the author about the train to Westhaven?
questions.zh: 时刻表上关于开往西黑文的那趟车告诉了他什么？
questions.a: It was an express train that went direct from his local station, and the journey would last a mere hour and seventeen minutes.
questions.aZh: 那是一趟从他就近的车站直达的快车，全程仅需1小时17分钟。
questions.hint: 出处：'there was an express train to Westhaven. It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.'

questions.q: Why did the author not find it strange that many local people got on the same train?
questions.zh: 为什么许多当地人也上了这趟车，作者却并不觉得奇怪？
questions.a: He reflected that there must be a great many local people besides himself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
questions.aZh: 他当时想，除他之外，一定还有很多当地人想利用这趟优质列车之便。
questions.hint: 出处：'I reflected that there must be a great many local people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.'

questions.q: How did the author finally find out the truth about the train?
questions.zh: 作者最终是怎样发现这趟车的真相的？
questions.a: The station master glanced briefly at the timetable and told him to look again; a tiny asterisk conducted him to a footnote at the bottom of the page, which said the service had been suspended.
questions.aZh: 站长迅速扫了一眼时刻表，让他再看一遍；一个小小的星号把他引向该页底部的脚注，上面写着此趟列车已暂停运行。
questions.hint: 出处：'A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page. It said: "This service has been suspended."'

questions.q: What does the story suggest about trusting timetables and blaming the railway authorities?
questions.zh: 这个故事对我们'信任时刻表'和'责怪铁路当局'说明了什么？
questions.a: It suggests we should read carefully and check the small print: when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs, so it is all too easy—and unfair—to blame the railway authorities.
questions.aZh: 它说明我们应当细读、留意那些小字：出了差错，多半是我们自己而非铁路当局的错，因此怪罪铁路部门往往既轻率又不公平。
questions.hint: 出处：'when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.'

translation:
我们已经习惯于相信火车总是准点的。
经过多年的适应，大多数人对火车时刻表产生了一种不可动摇的信念。
轮船船期可能因风暴而推延，飞机航班可能因恶劣天气而取消，唯有火车必然是准点的。
只有非同寻常的大雪才可能暂时打乱铁路运行。
因此，一旦铁路上真出了问题，人们便不加思索地责备铁路当局。
事实上，差错很可能是我们自己，而不是铁路当局的。
我查看了列车时刻表，满意地了解到有一趟去威斯特海温的快车。
这是趟直达车，旅途总共才需1小时17分钟。
上车后，我不禁注意到许多当地人也上了车。
一开始，我并不感到奇怪，我想除我之外，想利用快车之便的也一定大有人在。
火车开出几英里即在一个小站威德里停了下来。
对此，我不觉得奇怪，因为即便是特别快车也可能被信号拦住。
但是，当火车一站接着一站往前蠕动时，我便产生了怀疑。
我突然感到这趟快车并没以时速90英里的速度呼啸前进，而是卟哧卟哧地向前爬行，时速仅30英里。
1小时17分过去了，走了还不到一半路程。
我问一位乘客，这是不是开往威斯特海温的那趟快车，他说从未听说过有这么一趟快车。
我决定到目的地就给铁路部门提意见。
两小时后，我气呼呼地同威斯特海温站站长说起此事。
他说根本没有这趟车。
于是我借他本人的列车时刻表，我带着一种胜利者的调子告诉他那趟车白纸黑字。
明明白白印在时刻表上。
他迅速地扫视了一眼，让我再看一遍。
一个小小的星形符号把我的目光引到了那页底部一个说明上。
上面写着：“此趟列车暂停运行。”
title: The Westhaven Express
subtitle: 西黑文快车

lead.question: 作者为什么会坐上一趟早已停运的'西黑文快车'？他的错误究竟在哪里？
lead.warmup: 在英国人心里，火车几乎是准点的代名词：轮船会因风暴误期，飞机会因天气取消，唯有火车必须准点。久而久之，人们对时刻表产生了一种近乎迷信的信任。可这张纸上除了黑字，还常常藏着不起眼的星号和脚注。本课的作者就因为只顾看正表、忽略了那行小字，白白在慢车上耗了两个小时。
goals: 学会用 punctual、timetable、delay、suspend 等词谈论交通与时刻表
掌握 unshakable faith、take advantage of、in black and white 等固定搭配
复习被动语态：can be held up、has been suspended
理解 more likely … than 比较级结构，并用一般过去时叙述经历
lead.summary: 人们总相信火车必然准点，出了差错便怪罪铁路当局，其实错的往往是我们自己。作者查时刻表，发现有一趟开往西黑文的直达快车，全程仅1小时17分。上车后他并不觉得奇怪，可火车却一站站慢行。同车乘客没听说过这趟车，站长也否认它的存在；最后，一个星号把他引向脚注：此趟列车已暂停运行。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：'准时'是 be punctual，不要写成 be on punctual；can't help 后面接动名词，如 can't help noticing（不禁注意到），不能接动词原形。

exercises.q: 汉译英：经过多年的适应，大多数人对火车时刻表产生了不可动摇的信念。
exercises.a: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.

exercises.q: 改为被动语态：Signals can hold up even a mighty express train.
exercises.a: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
exercises.note: 情态动词被动 can be done

exercises.q: 用括号内动词的适当形式填空：Ships may be ______ (delay) by storms, and flights may be ______ (cancel) because of bad weather.
exercises.note: 情态动词后接被动语态

exercises.q: 改错：This service have been suspended.
汉译英，用 more likely … than：事实上，差错很可能是我们自己，而不是铁路当局的。
exercises.a: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.

exercises.q: 写出下列词的中文或英文：express, timetable, punctual, conductor
exercises.a: express 快车；timetable 时刻表；punctual 准时的；conductor 列车员

exercises.q: 用一般过去时填空：When I ______ (board) the train, I ______ (notice) that a great many local people ______ (get) on as well.
exercises.note: 一般过去时叙述过去动作

quiz.q: 什么原因可能暂时打乱铁路运行？
options: An exceptionally heavy snowfall.
A sudden storm at sea.
The cancellation of a flight.
A mistake in the timetable.
quiz.note: Only an exceptionally heavy snowfall…dislocate railway services.

quiz.q: 作者从时刻表中得知，开往西黑文的快车全程需要多久？
options: One hour and seventeen minutes.
Two hours exactly.
Ninety miles per hour.
Thirty minutes only.
quiz.note: the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes

quiz.q: 当火车一站接一站地慢下来时，作者察觉到了什么？
options: It was chugging along at barely thirty miles an hour.
It was roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour.
It had stopped for good at Widley.
It had taken a wrong line.
quiz.note: not…ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty

quiz.q: 作者问那位乘客时，对方是如何回答的？
options: He had not even heard of the Westhaven Express.
He said the train was held up by signals.
He confirmed that it was the express.
He advised him to get off at Widley.
quiz.note: he had not even heard of it

quiz.q: 站长为什么说根本没有这趟车？
options: Because the service had been suspended.
Because the timetable was printed wrongly.
Because the author had taken the wrong train.
Because the express runs only in winter.

quiz.q: 那个星号最终把作者引向了什么？
options: A footnote at the bottom of the page.
The address of the railway authority.
A later train in the timetable.
A complaint form at the station.
quiz.note: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote
